rationale: One anchor is still missing from the verification finding: its rationale leans on what the API promises, and I quoted that purpose without citing the range it comes from. That is the normative half of the finding - the behaviour is only a defect because the call is offered as a guard against serving stale data after losing leadership - so it should be anchored like the code half, not left as paraphrase. This adds the documentation range as a source and records the promise itself as a behaviour, so a reader can see the two sides of the comparison in the record: what the call is for, and what its count actually aggregates. Nothing else changes, no claim is added, and no execution is spent; this is the last thing I can complete inside the budget rather than another pass over the same ground.

knowledge.statement: The documentation for VerifyLeader states that it is used to ensure the peer is still the leader and may be used to prevent returning stale data from the FSM after the peer has lost leadership. That is the promise the verification count is measured against: the call is offered as a leadership guard for reads, so a successful verification is read by callers as evidence that this node may still answer as leader, which is why it matters that the count it aggregates can be satisfied by sources the voter quorum does not contain.
knowledge.conditions: This revision, the public VerifyLeader call as documented at the cited range; the statement records the documented purpose, and whether a given application relies on it that way is a property of the application.
